comment: Ballistic Dynamics cartridges: a projectile and its published muzzle velocity with the barrel it was measured in.

cartridges.name: .308 Win Federal Gold Medal Match 175 gr SMK (GM308M2)

provenance.muzzle_velocity_fps: published: Federal Premium catalogue, GM308M2, 2600 fps
provenance.test_barrel_in: published: Federal Premium ballistics are from a 24 in test barrel for .308 Win

cartridges.name: 6.5 Creedmoor Hornady Match 140 gr ELD Match (81500)

provenance.muzzle_velocity_fps: published: Lapua product page 4318017, 890 m/s (2920 fps)
provenance.test_barrel_in: estimated: Lapua's page does not state it here; CIP test barrels for .338 LM are about 690 mm (27.2 in)

provenance.muzzle_velocity_fps: published: Hornady, .50 BMG 750 gr A-MAX Match, 2820 fps
provenance.test_barrel_in: estimated: .50 BMG factory velocities are usually from 29-30 in barrels; Hornady's summary does not state it

cartridges.name: 5.56x45 mm Federal American Eagle XM855 62 gr

provenance.muzzle_velocity_fps: published: Federal XM855 load data, 3020 fps
provenance.test_barrel_in: estimated: a 20 in barrel, the M16A2 length 5.56 factory data is usually quoted for

cartridges.name: 9 mm Luger Speer Gold Dot 124 gr (23618GD)

provenance.muzzle_velocity_fps: published: CheyTac product page, .408/419 gr, 2752 fps (839 m/s)
provenance.test_barrel_in: estimated: the M200 Intervention's 29 in barrel, which CheyTac's figures are generally quoted from

cartridges.name: 6.5 Creedmoor Hornady Match 147 gr ELD Match (81501)

provenance.muzzle_velocity_fps: published: Hornady 81501, 2695 fps (as listed by retailers)
provenance.test_barrel_in: published: Hornady, 24 in test barrel (GAP Precision listing)

provenance.muzzle_velocity_fps: estimated: 865 m/s, the figure commonly quoted for the light ball from the M91/30's 730 mm barrel; not checked against a Soviet manual here
provenance.test_barrel_in: published: the M91/30 barrel, 730 mm (28.7 in)

provenance.muzzle_velocity_fps: published: (secondary) Wikipedia, SVD article, 830 m/s from the SVD; another source ties 830 m/s to the later 7N14, so 7N1 may be a few m/s slower
provenance.test_barrel_in: published: the SVD barrel, 620 mm (24.4 in)
